note: Conformance vectors for ontos-readable-json/1. Hand-authored from the spec page; input_hex and value_hex are derived by tools/json-projection/gen.mjs and every case is checked by tools/json-projection/check.mjs. Format: README.md beside this file.

cases.name: string-escaping
cases.note: the fixed escaping of readable §5: short escapes, \u00xx lowercase for other controls, everything else literal, / unescaped

cases.name: string-leading-feff
cases.note: U+FEFF inside a string is content

cases.name: string-no-normalization
cases.note: composed and decomposed é stay distinct

cases.name: negative-zero
cases.note: normalization negative-zero

cases.name: object-codec-order
cases.note: codec order: the shorter key first, so b before aa

cases.name: object-member-order
cases.note: normalization member-order; origins follow the members to their sorted entries

cases.name: object-bytewise-order
cases.note: equal lengths compare bytewise: Z (5A) before a (61)

cases.name: object-long-key-order
cases.note: from 128 bytes on the uvarint is not in numeric order: 256 (80 02) sorts before 129 (81 01)

cases.name: object-proto-keys
cases.note: __proto__ and constructor are data

cases.name: object-dollar-keys
cases.note: only $ontos is reserved: $bytes and $undefined are ordinary keys

cases.name: object-unnormalized-keys
cases.note: two keys that differ only by normalization are two keys; C3 A9 (2 bytes) sorts before 65 CC 81 (3 bytes)

cases.name: total-form-is-a-map-here
cases.note: the same text is Atom(0x00) under ontos-total-json/1 (readable §11)

cases.name: bytes-escaped-envelope
cases.note: the reserved name and the tag name are compared after escape decoding

cases.name: list-of-bytes
cases.note: a plain string that looks like base64 stays text

cases.name: int-tag-2pow127
cases.note: the smallest positive int beyond i128

cases.name: int-tag-small
cases.note: normalization tagged-small-int

cases.name: string-of-digits
cases.note: a string of digits is text

cases.name: decimal-one-is-not-int
cases.note: a decimal and an int of the same number are distinct values

cases.name: decimal-huge-exponent
cases.note: never expanded: the exponent stays an integer component

cases.name: map-non-text-keys
cases.note: normalization entry-order: an atom key (tag 00) sorts before a tuple key (tag 01)

cases.name: map-reserved-key
cases.note: the map from the text $ontos to null(): the map tag is the escape

cases.name: map-tag-text-keys
cases.note: normalization text-keyed-map

cases.name: map-int-keys-codec-order
cases.note: ints sort by encoding, not by number: 1 < -1 < 256

cases.name: set
cases.note: normalization entry-order

cases.name: set-heterogeneous
cases.note: an atom (tag 00) first; then int before utf8-text, whose label lengths are 3 and 9

cases.name: compound-empty-label
cases.note: Tuple(Atom(""))

cases.name: compound-non-utf8-label
cases.note: a label that is not UTF-8 is spelled as bytes

cases.name: compound-utf8-label-as-bytes
cases.note: normalization utf8-label

cases.name: compound-label-text-is-label-bytes
cases.note: a utf8-text-labelled tuple whose payload is not UTF-8 is no text: it is preserved as a compound

cases.name: malformed-decimal-preserved
cases.note: a non-canonical decimal-shaped tuple survives unrepaired

cases.name: malformed-int-preserved
cases.note: an int payload with a leading zero byte is no int

cases.name: unsorted-set-preserved
cases.note: sorting applies only to the set tag; a compound keeps its order

cases.name: compound-list-normalizes
cases.note: normalization preferred-spelling

cases.name: raw-children-stay-total
cases.note: inside raw the whole subtree is total form, so the int 1 is spelled node for node

cases.name: unsafe-in-object
cases.note: the advice's example

cases.name: base64-pad-bits
cases.note: AB== has non-zero pad bits; AA== is the byte 00

cases.name: envelope-extra-member-after
cases.note: an object with $ontos is exactly the envelope; it never falls back to a map

cases.name: unknown-tag-case
cases.note: tag names are case-sensitive

cases.name: raw-readable-child
cases.note: the children of a raw tuple are total form, not readable spellings

cases.name: compound-label-envelope
cases.note: the label position takes a string or ["bytes", …], never an envelope

cases.name: map-entries-before-keys
cases.note: every entry's shape is checked before any key is read

cases.name: map-duplicate-int-spellings
cases.note: 1 and the tagged 1 are one ground value

cases.name: map-duplicate-before-value
cases.note: the duplicate key is found before its value is read

cases.name: object-duplicate-before-number
cases.note: stage 3 refuses the repeated name before stage 4 reads 1.5

cases.name: truncated-before-number
cases.note: the text must be JSON before it is interpreted

cases.name: lists-1024-accepted
cases.note: 1024 nested lists: the innermost list's label atom lies at value depth 1024

cases.name: lists-1025-value-depth
cases.note: JSON depth 1025 passes stage 3; the innermost list's label would lie at value depth 1025

cases.name: compounds-1024-accepted
cases.note: 1024 compounds around a raw empty tuple: value depth 1024 and JSON depth 3076 = 3·1024 + 4, both at the defaults

cases.name: compounds-1025-json-depth
cases.note: the raw envelope's array opens at JSON depth 3077

cases.name: arrays-3076-then-value-depth
cases.note: 3076 nested arrays pass stage 3; stage 4 stops at the 1025th list

cases.name: json-depth-not-value-depth
cases.note: value depth 2 is within bounds; the spelling needs JSON depth 6

cases.name: value-depth-not-json-depth
cases.note: JSON depth 3 is within bounds; the value is nested 3 deep

cases.name: integer-digits-default-4300
cases.note: 4300 digits, the default bound

cases.name: write-integer-digits-default
cases.note: under the defaults the writer will not spell a 4301-digit integer in decimal

cases.name: atom-bytes-label
cases.note: label atoms count: utf8-text is 9 bytes

cases.name: limit-tuple-arity
cases.note: a list of three is a tuple of arity four

cases.name: write-mirror-object-first
cases.note: two bounds are exceeded; the object's contribution, its 20-byte key included, is checked before its first byte, so atom_bytes refuses before the nested list reaches depth 5

cases.name: read-mirror-object-first
cases.note: the reader refuses the writer's text with the same kind

cases.name: json-depth-derived
cases.note: max_json_depth unset is derived as 3·0 + 4 = 4

cases.name: multibyte-before-span
cases.note: é is two bytes, so the span is [6, 9); UTF-16 code units would give [5, 8)

cases.name: multibyte-key-origins
cases.note: a raw two-byte key: spans count bytes

cases.name: high-surrogate-then-bad-escape
cases.note: the next six bytes are not an escape naming a low surrogate

cases.name: int-tag-non-ascii-digit
cases.note: U+0662 is a digit to some conversions (Python's int()), never to int-text

cases.name: contrib-null-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: null() contributes its tuple at d and its label atom at d + 1; accepted at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-null-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: null() contributes its tuple at d and its label atom at d + 1; refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-null-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-bool-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: a bool contributes its tuple at d and its two atoms at d + 1; accepted at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-bool-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: a bool contributes its tuple at d and its two atoms at d + 1; refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-bool-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-string-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-number-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: an integer literal contributes int's tuple at d and its two atoms at d + 1; refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-number-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-array-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: an array contributes the list tuple at d and its label atom at d + 1; accepted at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-array-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: an array contributes the list tuple at d and its label atom at d + 1; refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-array-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 0

cases.name: contrib-array-element-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: array elements are interpreted at d + 1; accepted at max_value_depth 2

cases.name: contrib-array-element-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: array elements are interpreted at d + 1; refused at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-array-element-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-object-empty-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: an empty object contributes the map tuple at d and its label atom at d + 1; accepted at max_value_depth 1

cases.name: contrib-object-keys-at-bound

cases.name: contrib-object-keys-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: an object contributes each key text's tuple at d + 2 and its atoms at d + 3; refused at max_value_depth 2

cases.name: contrib-object-keys-write-below
cases.note: the writer mirrors the reader (total §9.3): refused at max_value_depth 2

cases.name: contrib-object-keys-deepest-at-bound
cases.note: readable §4.9: the member value is an atom at d + 2, so the keys' atoms at d + 3 are the deepest contribution; accepted at max_value_depth 3

cases.name: contrib-object-keys-deepest-below
cases.note: readable §4.9: the member value is an atom at d + 2, so the keys' atoms at d + 3 are the deepest contribution; refused at max_value_depth 2

cases.name: contrib-set-of-bytes-at-bound

cases.name: contrib-set-of-bytes-write-below
